title: Grain Clerk Training Note: Where the Carry Clock Starts on an Unpriced Parcel
content:
The carry anchor on bushels standing unpriced under Grain Marketing Contracts moves with what happened to the grain before it began to stand unpriced. Three cases arise, and they are read in the order set out below.

**First.** Where a handling shrink adjustment on conditioned bushels stands against the member's storage account under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements, the carry clock runs from the day that handling shrink adjustment was taken, since grain that is still being conditioned is not yet standing at the member's cost.

**Second.** Where no such adjustment stands and the parcel entered the unpriced position before the first day of the contract's delivery window, the carry clock runs from the first day of the contract's delivery window.

**Third.** Where neither of those holds, the carry clock runs from the day the parcel entered the member's unpriced position.

## The three cases in one view

| A handling shrink adjustment on conditioned bushels standing on the storage account | The parcel entered the unpriced position before the first day of the delivery window | The clock runs from |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either way | the day that adjustment was taken |
| No | Yes | the first day of the delivery window |
| No | No | the day the parcel entered the unpriced position |

## Illustration on hypothetical records

A member's storage account under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements carries a shrink adjustment on conditioned bushels dated the tenth of a month, and the parcel took its place in the unpriced position on the first of that month. The clock runs from the tenth, and the day the parcel entered the unpriced position does not govern. Where no such adjustment stands and the parcel entered the unpriced position a fortnight before the delivery window opened, the clock runs from the first day of that window instead.
